questions.stem: What type of current does an AC generator (alternator) produce?

options.text: Direct current that flows in one direction only
Alternating current that reverses direction periodically
Pulsed current that stops and starts
Static charge that builds up on the coil

questions.explanation: An AC generator (alternator) produces alternating current, which continuously reverses direction. As the coil rotates in the magnetic field, the direction of the induced current changes every half rotation, creating a sinusoidal output.

questions.stem: What is the key structural difference between an AC generator and a DC generator?

options.text: An AC generator uses stronger magnets
A DC generator uses slip rings instead of a commutator
An AC generator uses slip rings while a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator
A DC generator does not need brushes

questions.explanation: The key difference is in how they connect the coil to the external circuit. An AC generator uses continuous slip rings, allowing the current to alternate. A DC generator uses a split-ring commutator that reverses connections every half turn, producing current that always flows in one direction.
